laboratory noun

also lab, language lab

classical

Cic. Off. 1.150; Caes. BC 1.34 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. laboratory, after Grosse (1846) and Egger
Levi–Bini p. 36: laboratorio

officīna, officīnae f.

noun, first declension

a workshop; a laboratory

A workshop of any trade, contracted from opificīna (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens and Levi and Bini give it for the scientist’s laboratory too.

Other words

  • labōrātōrium, labōrātōriī n.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. laboratory, after Egger; Andresian p. 43

    From labōrāre; not in Lewis & Short. Egger uses it with “as they call it”.

Examples

  • officīna loquēlāris

    a language labTraupman 337

See also office.
